name: Shadowfax Technologies Ltd
title: Shadowfax Technologies Ltd - 544685 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Shadowfax grew FY26 revenue 69% to INR 4,200 crores+ with adjusted EBITDA near INR 159 crores, but management is raising capex and guiding 100–120 bps margin gains to FY28 with no supply discipline evidence.

summary.headline: Shadowfax Q4 FY26 revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY) with record 4.5% PAT margin; FY26 PAT INR 112 crores.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q4 FY26 growth and profitability: revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY, +6.7% QoQ), adjusted EBITDA about INR 58 crores (4.7% margin vs 4.3% in Q3 and 0.7% a year ago) and PAT INR 56 crores (4.5% margin). For FY26, revenue exceeded INR 4,200 crores (+69%), adjusted EBITDA was about INR 159 crores (roughly 3x FY25) and PAT was INR 112 crores vs INR 6 crores. Management guided to 27-30% overall growth, 100-120 bps adjusted EBITDA margin improvement through FY28, and FY27 capex of INR 180-190 crores, while investing in real estate, dark stores and large-shipment coverage.

financial_highlights.change: vs 4.3% in Q3 FY26 and 0.7% in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Express parcel
segments.commentary: About 75% of revenue; management says it is gaining share via new client wins, deeper engagement and value-added services such as same-day, next-day and reverse logistics. Top 2-3 customer concentration unchanged QoQ.

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Grew more than 50% YoY and 16% QoQ in Q4; quick commerce volumes picked up and operations with Amazon Now commenced. Management guides 45-50% growth for this segment in the next year.

segments.name: Other logistics services
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 80 crores of the INR 1,200-plus crores quarterly revenue; wind-down of experimental services is largely complete as of Q4 FY26, with reshaping towards critical logistics.

guidance_outlook: Overall business growth guidance maintained at 27-30%; hyperlocal expected at 45-50% YoY.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 100-120 bps over the next couple of years through FY28; 200-250 bps per year after FY28 until steady-state EBITDA.
Steady-state adjusted EBITDA margin viewed as sustainable at early double digits.
FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crores, flat in absolute terms vs FY26; dark stores to be less than 10% of capex.
Pin code coverage to rise from 15,600 (of 19,300) to about 17,000 by end FY27 and full country coverage by FY28; large-shipment pin codes from about 6,000 to 10,000 in FY27.
Plans to set up about 100 dark stores in FY27 for vertical quick commerce (about 15 today).
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crores, flat in absolute terms vs FY26; dark stores less than 10% of capex.
Real estate footprint up 35% between September 2025 and March 2026 (leased last-mile and middle-mile sortation centres).
Touch points rose from 4,200 to 4,700 in about six months; opening about 120-150 pin codes per month.
OneNCR, one of the largest sorting centres, went live a few months back after about six months of dual costs; new last-mile hubs take six to eight months to reach efficiency.
Over the last three years more than 60% of capex went to sorting centres and about 85% to sorting centres plus last-mile hubs; strategy is to run a dual manual/automated setup.
demand_pricing: 3PL market share estimated at about 28-29% for Q4, up from about 17-18% a year earlier; growth split roughly 50-55% market growth and 40-45% share gains.
D2C and SME grew about 2.5x between FY25 and FY26; pricing 15-20% higher than enterprise customers; sales team expanded by more than 100 people.
Large-shipment business grew 3-4x vs FY25; currently serving about 6,000 pin codes.
Quick commerce: management says it maintains pricing as largest 3PL in the segment; works with six to seven QC platforms.
Lost shipments and QC debits about 6.1% of revenue in Q4 (6.3% in Q3, 5.7% in FY25); long-term target 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Where is market share gain coming from, and will it stabilise by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gains come from inefficient traditional 3PLs and some captive insourcing reversing; the top two players are gaining share and the market is consolidating. It did not give a stabilisation date.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY26 margin expansion look better as capex normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said significant operating leverage is yet to come, with opex from investments returning in FY27-FY28, and that H2 capex was made in advance for FY27 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Dark store unit economics and ROIC?
qa_highlights.answer: Top dark stores run at about 20%+ gross margin; breakeven in three to four months; average revenue INR 8-15 lakh per store per month; ROIC too early to quantify with 15 pilot stores.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance basis and service EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is on adjusted EBITDA only; management does not track service EBITDA. Part of the improvement comes from corporate operating leverage, with the rest from service EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Lost shipment cost and white goods impact?
qa_highlights.answer: About half of the roughly 6% is quality-check debits from reverse logistics and half pure losses; management cited image-recognition upgrades and fixes in large-parcel damages in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Amazon Shipping and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said captive arms deprioritise external customers at peak, so they do not see such models working in India; D2C/SME is a meaningful double-digit share of revenue, not disclosed exactly.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and crude price volatility; fuel is under 10% of costs and contracts carry fuel surcharges, but customer demand for logistics could slow if fuel rises sharply.
Lost shipments and QC debits at about 6.1% of revenue, well above the 4-5% long-term goal; white goods expansion could add to losses.
Dual-cost drag from new sorting centres and last-mile hubs (six to eight months ramp) could weigh on near-term margins.
Hyperlocal YoY growth slowed in Q4 due to a strong prior-year Q4 base; competition in quick commerce crowdsourcing from platforms like LoadShare.
Dark store ROIC not yet proven at scale; 100-store target in FY27 is a new vertical.
Lower average shipment volume (volumetric weight) reduced realisation QoQ, per analyst question on yield dip.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, margins and the long-term network model, with strong claims on share gains and AI. Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to split D2C revenue, dark-store ROIC, service EBITDA and client-level profitability, and kept guidance deliberately limited to adjusted EBITDA.
key_quotes: We believe in a business like this, early double -digit steady -state EBITDA margins are sustainable.
Our long-term goal was to bring it down to about 4% to 5%.
We don't talk about service EBITDA. We don't look at service EBITDA. We only look at adjusted EBITDA and that's what we are guiding everyone for.
Whatever we are growing today, whatever we are forecasting, I think 50%, 55% we are attributing to the underlying growth in 3PL market.

adds.what: About 100 dark stores for vertical quick commerce in FY27 (about 15 today)
Pin code coverage from 15,600 to about 17,000 by end FY27 (touch points 4,200 to 4,700 in about six months, opening 120-150 pin codes per month)
Large-shipment pin codes from about 6,000 to 10,000 in FY27

growth.why: Management maintained 27-30% overall growth guidance for FY27 (midpoint 28.5%), with hyperlocal guided at 45-50%, backed by pin code expansion to about 17,000, about 100 new dark stores, and a 3PL share gain from 17-18% to 28-29%, though no firm order book was quantified.
